# DocSync — Approach

## What we are building

A diff-based doc freshness feature: surface documentation sections that have drifted out of sync with the code they describe, shown as a CLI warning during normal dev workflow.

## Who it is for

Solo developers and small teams already using DocSync to generate codemaps.

## Why

Docs silently rot; the biggest pain is not writing docs but trusting that existing docs are still true. Treating freshness as a diffing problem (code changed, doc did not) lets us flag staleness automatically.

## Product decisions already settled

- Freshness is surfaced as a non-blocking CLI warning, not a hard failure.
- Scope is limited to Markdown docs under ./docs; source-code comments are out of scope.
- A section is 'stale' when the code paths it references changed after the doc's last edit.

# Ideation report — 2026-05-20

## Desired Outcome

Make developers trust that docs are current without manual review.

## Opportunities

### Diff-based doc freshness score (adjacent)

**Idea** Surface stale documentation sections as a CLI warning, scored by how far the referenced code has drifted since the doc was last touched.

**Why this codebase is uniquely positioned** DocSync already builds a code-to-doc reference map when generating codemaps; the freshness check reuses that map.

**Audience** Existing DocSync users on solo/small-team projects.

assertions.text: The agent reads ./docs/approach.md before starting the interview (step 1)
The agent reads the ./ideas/reports/2026-05-20-ideate.md report before starting the interview (step 1)
The agent does NOT ask the user to describe the problem from scratch (step 1) — the problem is already captured in the priors
The agent does NOT re-interview on scope/audience/product decisions already settled in the priors (e.g. does not re-ask whether the warning should block, or who the audience is)
Any grilling (step 3, via grill-with-docs) is confined to genuine deltas or gaps not answered by the priors, not a full re-interview
The final PRD's Problem Statement and Solution are consistent with the approach doc and ideate report (diff-based doc freshness, non-blocking CLI warning, Markdown-only scope)
The PRD is created as a GitHub issue titled with a [PRD] prefix
The PRD stays in product language only — no code, schema, file paths, or library choices in the body

evals.name: nothing-on-disk-full-interview
evals.prompt: I want to write a PRD for a new feature, but I haven't written anything down yet.
evals.expected_output: With no ./docs/approach.md and no ./ideas/reports/*-ideate.md on disk, the skill falls back to the full interview unchanged: it asks the user for a detailed problem description (step 1), explores the repo (step 2), and grills via grill-with-docs (step 3) before writing the PRD.

assertions.text: The agent asks the user for a long, detailed description of the problem (step 1) — the full interview runs because no priors are on disk
The agent does NOT claim to have loaded an approach doc or ideate report that does not exist — it does not fabricate priors
The agent explores the repo to ground the PRD (step 2)
The agent runs the grilling session via the grill-with-docs skill (step 3), not a re-inlined questioning loop
The PRD is created as a GitHub issue titled with a [PRD] prefix
The PRD stays in product language only — no code, schema, file paths, or library choices in the body
